adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded remote fetch with no timeout: open(url).read in lib/topic_retriever.rb / app/models/topic_embed.rb:53 and open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 lack open_timeout/read_timeout and a size cap, allowing attacker-supplied or slow URLs to pin Sidekiq workers and materialize arbitrarily large responses in memory

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces multiple remote fetches via `open-uri` without any timeout or response-size limiting: `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, and `open(url).read` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (used by `TopicRetriever#fetch_http`). Since `embed_url` ultimately comes from the request (`EmbedController#best` enqueues `retrieve_topic` with `embed_url`), a slow/large response from an allowed host can pin Sidekiq workers and potentially consume excessive memory.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded feed-item import loop: poll_feed.rb:31-37 iterates every feed item with no limit or stop-at-seen logic, issuing a DB query and full-content SHA1 per item every hour even when unchanged; the feed_key/feed-modified cache is defined but never used

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `poll_feed` does `rss.items.each` with no cap and no “stop when already-seen” logic, and each iteration calls `TopicEmbed.import`, which computes `Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(contents)` and performs at least one lookup (`TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first`). This will re-scan the entire feed hourly even if nothing changed. Additionally, `feed_key` is defined (intended for caching/modified tracking) but is never referenced anywhere in the diff, so no conditional fetch/early-exit is implemented.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Imported embed content bypasses the sanitizer: raw_html cook returns raw unsanitized HTML that is served to embed viewers (raw post.cooked in best.html.erb), and Readability + absolutize_urls double-parses arbitrary remote HTML through Nokogiri in the worker

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly introduces a `raw_html` cook path that bypasses the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline: `Post#cook` now returns `raw` when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (app/models/post.rb). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents)` (app/models/topic_embed.rb), and the embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb). `absolutize_urls` only rewrites URLs via Nokogiri and does not sanitize potentially dangerous tags/attributes, so arbitrary HTML from RSS (`PollFeed` uses `i.content`) or remote fetch (`import_remote` uses `doc.content`) can be served to embed viewers unsanitized, which is a verifiable security defect (XSS). The mention of Readability + Nokogiri “double-parsing” is also consistent with `import_remote` + `absolutize_urls`, though the core issue is the sanitizer bypass.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Potential N+1 in embed view: embed/best.html.erb:14-16 accesses post.user per post (up to 5), possibly triggering per-post user loads if TopicView doesn't eager-load authors

adjudication.rationale: In app/views/embed/best.html.erb the loop renders up to 5 posts and accesses post.user.small_avatar_url and post.user.username per post. If @topic_view.posts does not eager-load the associated users, this pattern can cause an N+1 query when rendering the embed page. The diff doesn’t show TopicView’s preload behavior, so it’s a performance risk rather than a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unsanitized external HTML from RSS feeds and embed URLs is stored as `cooked` (bypassing the cooking/sanitization pipeline) and exposed in API responses, causing XSS across a trust boundary (topic_embed.rb:11-16, post.rb:128-131, embed/best.html.erb:16)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces an explicit bypass of Discourse’s cooking/sanitization pipeline for imported/embed content: `Post#cook` now returns `raw` when `cook_method == :raw_html` (app/models/post.rb), and `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` using `contents` sourced from RSS (`Jobs::PollFeed` uses `i.content`/`i.title` from `SimpleRSS.parse open(...)`) or remote HTML (`TopicEmbed.import_remote` parses `open(url).read`). The embed UI then renders this HTML with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb), which will execute any unsafe markup/scripts present in the imported content. This is a verifiable XSS risk across a trust boundary introduced by the change (even if `ruby-readability` filters tags, PollFeed path does not sanitize, and URL schemes like `javascript:` are not shown to be blocked).

adjudication_records.issue_text: SQL/HTML injection via attacker-controlled `embed_url` interpolated into a single-quoted href attribute in topic_embed.rb:13; the http(s) regex check doesn't prevent breaking out with a quote, enabling stored XSS

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/topic_embed.rb` inside `TopicEmbed.import`, `url` is interpolated directly into a single-quoted HTML attribute: `"#{url}"`. The only validation is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent quotes (e.g. `http://example.com/' onclick='...`) from breaking out of the `href` attribute. Because imported posts can be created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `Post#cook` returns `raw` unchanged for that method, this can result in stored XSS if a malicious RSS/Atom feed (or other importer input) supplies a crafted `url`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Referer check in embed_controller.rb:25 is a weak/forgeable authorization gate for the new public `embed/best` route, and URI(referer).host may not match embeddable_host with port/scheme

adjudication.rationale: `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` authorizes access to the public `GET /embed/best` route solely by checking `URI(request.referer || '').host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host` (and then sets `X-Frame-Options = ALLOWALL`). Because `Referer` is a client-supplied header, this is a weak/forgeable gate and can be bypassed by non-browser clients (or situations where referer is suppressed/modified), undermining the intended embedding restriction. Also, the comparison uses only `.host`, so any configuration that expects port/scheme matching (or stores more than a bare hostname) would not be enforced by this check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Breaking CLI contract change in disqus.thor:117 — removing the `-c/--category` option breaks existing scripts, category routing silently dropped, and content source changed to full remote-page fetch altering dry_run output

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` removes `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` and all related `category_id` logic, so `-c/--category` is no longer accepted and posts can no longer be routed to a specified category via this CLI (breaking backward compatibility). It also changes import behavior from creating a post with a simple permalink raw (`PostCreator.new(... raw: "[[Permalink](...)]" ...)`) to fetching and embedding remote page content via `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`. However, the claim that this “alters dry_run output” is not verifiable from the diff because the remote fetch occurs only inside `if options[:dry_run].blank?` (i.e., not in dry-run).

adjudication_records.issue_text: postMessage origin check in embed.js:18 uses substring match (indexOf) instead of origin equality, accepting origins like forum.example.com.attacker.tld and rejecting legitimate http/https or trailing-slash variants
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments flag the same underlying vulnerability: using indexOf/substring matching for postMessage origin validation allows bypass via attacker-controlled domains that include the trusted domain as a substring (e.g., evil-discourseUrl.com or forum.example.com.attacker.tld).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `force: true` added to the already-shipped create_table :top_topics migration can silently drop existing table data on deployments that re-run migrations

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration (20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb) from `create_table :top_topics` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists and recreate it, which can cause data loss if this migration is ever executed against a DB where `top_topics` already exists (e.g., migration re-run/redo or inconsistent schema state). This risk is introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed crashes with NoMethodError on RSS items without content (nil CGI.unescapeHTML input), and retry: false means one malformed item aborts the entire hourly feed poll

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the loop does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If an RSS item has `i.content == nil` (which is plausible across feeds), calling `.scrub` on nil will raise `NoMethodError`, aborting the entire `poll_feed` run. Since the job is configured with `sidekiq_options retry: false`, that failed execution will not be retried by Sidekiq, so one malformed item can prevent importing any subsequent items until the next scheduled run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Enum indexing of Post.cook_methods may mismatch migration default cook_method=1; if regular maps to 0, all existing posts silently switch to raw_html cooking — verify before merge

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `Post.cook_methods ||= Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)` and a migration setting `posts.cook_method` default to `1` (`add_cook_method_to_posts.rb`). The logic in `Post#cook` treats `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` as a special case and otherwise cooks normally. Whether `1` corresponds to `:regular` or `:raw_html` depends on how `Enum.new` indexes values (not shown in this diff). So the finding is a valid, diff-grounded risk to verify, but it’s not a defect that can be conclusively proven from the provided changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbedController#best raises 500 on deleted/missing topics because TopicView is constructed with stale topic_id without existence/visibility checks

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, if TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url) returns an id, the code unconditionally constructs TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5}) with no check that the topic still exists or is visible to the current user (no lookup/guard/rescue). Since topic_id_for_embed is a plain pluck from topic_embeds, it can return a stale topic_id if the topic/post was deleted or access-restricted, which would likely raise (e.g., RecordNotFound/permission error) and produce a 500.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PostRevisor#revise! contract change: @post.save now respects skip_validations, silently bypassing validations for existing callers, and blank-line removal changes should_revise? return behavior

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes PostRevisor#update_post from `@post.save` to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, meaning `skip_validations: true` now actually bypasses validations during revisions. That is a real behavioral/contract change with potential risk (invalid data) and should be scrutinized. However, the claim that the removed blank line changes `should_revise?` return behavior is unfounded—only whitespace was removed around `return false if not should_revise?`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/models/topic_embed.rb:47` `import_remote`: `open(url).read` uses open-uri with no timeout, so a slow upstream site blocks the RetrieveTopic Sidekiq worker indefinitely and can exhaust worker threads and stall the background queue

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/topic_embed.rb#import_remote, the code does `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` without specifying any open/read timeouts. This method is invoked from background processing paths added in the diff (TopicRetriever#fetch_http via Jobs::RetrieveTopic, and also used in disqus.thor). A slow/hung upstream HTTP response can block the Sidekiq worker thread for an unbounded time, reducing available workers and potentially stalling the queue. This availability risk is directly introduced by the new network fetch logic in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:27`: `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` has no timeout, and since this is an hourly scheduled job, a wedged feed URL repeatedly wedges workers

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added scheduled job `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` performs a network fetch via `open-uri` without any `open_timeout`/`read_timeout` or other bounding. If the feed endpoint stalls (e.g., hangs during connect or read), the Sidekiq worker executing this hourly job can block indefinitely, reducing worker capacity and potentially causing repeated hangs on subsequent runs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:10,26-32`: `sidekiq_options retry: false` with no exception handling means any exception (bad feed XML, network error, nil `i.content` in `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`) permanently aborts the entire poll and all later retries

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the job is explicitly configured with `sidekiq_options retry: false` and performs network + parsing work (`open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`, `SimpleRSS.parse`, then `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`) without any rescue/guarding. If `open` fails, parsing raises, or `i.content` is nil (calling `scrub`), the job will raise and abort processing the rest of the feed items; with `retry: false` Sidekiq will not automatically retry that failed execution.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed: if item 50 of 100 raises, items 1-49 are imported but 51-100 are silently skipped

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `rss.items.each do |i| ... TopicEmbed.import(...) end` has no per-item `rescue`, so any exception while processing an item (e.g., `i.content` nil, `scrub` missing, import raising) will abort the whole job mid-loop. Because the job sets `sidekiq_options retry: false`, remaining items after the failure will not be processed on that run, leading to partial import (e.g., items 1-49 imported, 50 raises, 51-100 not processed). The “silently” part is less certain (Sidekiq will log an error), but the skip/partial-import behavior is real from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed: the cached `feed_key` dedup state is never used (dead code), so every successful poll re-imports/re-renders every item

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the `feed_key` method is defined but never referenced anywhere in `execute`/`poll_feed`, so any intended cached/dedup state is indeed dead code. However, the claim that this causes every poll to "re-import/re-render every item" is overstated: `TopicEmbed.import` checks for an existing `TopicEmbed` by `embed_url` and only revises the post when `content_sha1` changes. The real issue grounded in the diff is wasted work (always fetching/parsing the feed and iterating items) and unused code, not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed: a single transient network blip loses an entire hour's worth of imports with no alert and no recovery

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the job does a direct `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with no error handling and sets `sidekiq_options retry: false`. A transient network/parse failure would cause the hourly run to fail and Sidekiq will not retry that execution, meaning imports for that cycle are skipped until the next scheduled run, with no built-in recovery mechanism (no persisted checkpoint/last-fetched marker) and no explicit alerting logic in the job.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `lib/topic_retriever.rb:20-27`: non-atomic `setnx`/`expire` — if the process dies between the two calls the throttle key exists forever with no TTL, permanently wedging retrieval for non-staff users

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` the throttle uses `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by a separate `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. If the process/thread crashes after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the key will persist without a TTL, causing `setnx` to fail forever thereafter and making `retrieved_recently?` return `true` permanently for non-staff users (wedging retrieval). This is directly verifiable from the diff in `lib/topic_retriever.rb`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `lib/topic_retriever.rb`: the permanent throttle key causes the embed page to show 'Loading Discussion...' indefinitely, with loading.html.erb reloading every 30s and re-enqueuing another doomed job

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?`, the throttle is implemented as `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by a separate `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. Because these are not atomic, a crash/timeout between the two calls can leave `retrieved:<embed_url>` without an expiry (effectively permanent). In that state `retrieved_recently?` will keep returning `true`, so `retrieve` will never call `perform_retrieve`, leaving `EmbedController#best` to keep rendering `loading` (and `loading.html.erb` reloads every 30s, re-enqueuing more jobs that remain throttled).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3`: `force: true` on a pre-existing migration means re-running it silently drops the table and all its rows (data-loss hazard)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration to `create_table :top_topics, force: true` (db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb). In Rails, `force: true` drops the table if it already exists before creating it, so re-running this migration (or running it in an environment where `top_topics` already exists) can silently delete all rows in `top_topics`, matching the data-loss hazard described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:13-16`: every `embed/best` request for an unknown URL enqueues a RetrieveTopic job with no request-level throttle or circuit breaker, allowing unbounded job enqueue by crawlers or for permanently unretrievable URLs

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is nil, it unconditionally does `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading`. There is no request-level throttling/circuit breaker before enqueue. While `TopicRetriever#retrieve` (invoked inside the `RetrieveTopic` job) implements a 60s Redis throttle in `retrieved_recently?`, that throttle only prevents the actual fetch, not the creation of Sidekiq jobs. Therefore repeated `GET /embed/best?embed_url=...` requests can enqueue an unbounded number of `RetrieveTopic` jobs (especially with varying URLs), which is a real resource-exhaustion/DoS risk introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `embed/best` loading page: loading.html.erb reloads every 30 seconds indefinitely with no backoff or max attempts and no failure state — a permanently unretrievable URL produces an infinite job-enqueue loop for as long as the iframe stays open

adjudication.rationale: `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb` unconditionally reloads the iframe every 30s with no max attempts or failure UI. In `EmbedController#best`, when no embed exists it always `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders `loading`, so each reload re-hits `embed/best` and enqueues another job. Although `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` throttles actual retrieval work, the diff still shows an unbounded job-enqueue loop for permanently-unretrievable URLs as long as the iframe remains open.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:14`: `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)` has no guard for deleted/missing topics, so a deleted topic raises a 500 inside the embed iframe on the customer's blog page

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when `topic_id` is returned from `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)`, the code directly calls `TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5})` with no check that the referenced `Topic` still exists. Since `topic_id_for_embed` is just a DB lookup on `topic_embeds` (`pluck(:topic_id).first`) and the diff shows no `dependent: :destroy`/FK cleanup to prevent stale `topic_embeds` after a topic is deleted, this is a concrete edge-case gap introduced by the new embedding flow. Whether it actually becomes a 500 depends on `TopicView` behavior (not shown), so the specific failure mode can’t be fully verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Topic deletion doesn't clean up `topic_embeds` rows (no dependent destroy/hook), so stale embeds accumulate

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `topic_embeds` table with a unique index on `embed_url` and a `TopicEmbed` model that `belongs_to :topic` / `belongs_to :post`, but it does not add any `dependent: :destroy` relationship from `Topic`/`Post` (nor any cleanup hook) in this diff, and the migration has no foreign keys/cascades. This makes orphaned `topic_embeds` rows plausible if topics/posts are hard-deleted, which is a concrete lifecycle/maintenance concern introduced by the new table, but the diff does not show topic deletion behavior so the impact cannot be verified as an immediate defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `lib/topic_retriever.rb:39-42`: `perform_retrieve` runs the full RSS poll synchronously via `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` on every embed retrieval miss, duplicating the hourly scheduler's work and lengthening job runtime

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/topic_retriever.rb` `perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true (and only after confirming the specific `@embed_url` has no existing `TopicEmbed`). This means each embed-miss retrieval will synchronously run a full feed poll before attempting `fetch_http`, which can duplicate the scheduled hourly poll (`Jobs::PollFeed < Jobs::Scheduled`) and increase the runtime of the `retrieve_topic` job path. This is a performance/architecture concern shown by the diff, not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `perform_retrieve`: because PollFeed has `retry: false` but here an exception inside it propagates into RetrieveTopic's retry logic, one bad feed can fail unrelated per-URL retrievals repeatedly

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true it directly calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` and does not rescue any exceptions (`lib/topic_retriever.rb`). `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` performs network I/O via `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and parsing (`SimpleRSS.parse`), both of which can raise. Because this invocation is inline (not enqueued through Sidekiq), `PollFeed`'s `sidekiq_options retry: false` does not apply, so any exception will bubble up and fail the `RetrieveTopic` job (`app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb`), which is likely retried by default. This can cause per-URL retrievals to fail/retry repeatedly due to a bad feed poll, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/models/topic_embed.rb:9-38`: on the update path, `revisor.revise!` and `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, ...)` are not wrapped in a transaction — if `update_column` fails after a successful revision, the sha1 mismatch causes the same revision to be re-applied on every subsequent poll

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path (`else` branch) applies a revision via `revisor.revise!(...)` and then separately persists the new checksum with `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` without a transaction. If the second DB write fails (e.g., transient DB error) after the post revision succeeds, `embed.content_sha1` remains stale, so subsequent polls will keep entering the `if content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1` branch and re-apply the revision.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `topic_embed.rb` `update_column` bypasses `updated_at`, so stale rows are invisible

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, when content changes it does `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)`, which updates only that column and skips normal timestamp updating (including `updated_at`). The diff does not show any code that queries `topic_embeds` by `updated_at` or depends on it for visibility, so the claim about “stale rows are invisible” isn’t verifiable here, but the timestamp-bypass is a concrete, diff-grounded concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:18`: origin check via substring match `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` allows origins containing the discourse URL as a substring, and trailing-slash/port mismatches may drop legitimate resize messages, leaving the iframe stuck at default height

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, the message handler validates the sender with `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`. This is not an exact origin comparison; it depends on `discourseUrl` string formatting and can reject legitimate messages (e.g., `e.origin` including an explicit port like `:443` while `discourseUrl` omits it) which would prevent `iframe.height` from being updated and leave the embed stuck at its default height. The check is also a weak security predicate because it relies on substring containment rather than comparing parsed origins.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/models/topic_embed.rb:11`: unescaped URL interpolated into HTML `href='#{url}'` — the `^https?://` regex permits quote characters, and with `skip_validations: true` cooking and `raw post.cooked` rendering this is an XSS path into the embed page, bypassing Discourse's sanitization pipeline

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code appends `...#{url}...` to `contents` after only checking `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which validates only the prefix and does not prevent quotes/angle brackets in the remainder of the URL. That HTML is then stored via `PostCreator` with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true`, and `Post#cook` explicitly returns `raw` for `raw_html`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. Finally, the embed view renders `raw post.cooked` (`app/views/embed/best.html.erb`), so a crafted `embed_url` (e.g., containing `%27` to become `'` after param decoding) can break out of the single-quoted `href` attribute and inject script/event handlers into the embed page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26-31`: `rescue URI::InvalidURIError` placement means `X-Frame-Options` is never set when the referer URI is invalid

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, `response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = 'ALLOWALL'` is only set after the referer host validation passes. If `URI(request.referer || '')` raises `URI::InvalidURIError`, the rescue re-raises `Discourse::InvalidAccess`, so the request is rejected; not setting `X-Frame-Options` on a rejected/errored request is expected and does not constitute a defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `layouts/embed.html.erb:11`: postMessage target uses `request.referer`; an invalid/missing/suppressed referer makes the postMessage a no-op, silently breaking iframe auto-resize

adjudication.rationale: In `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb` the iframe sends `parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>')`. The second argument to `postMessage` is `targetOrigin`, which must be an origin (scheme+host+port) or `*`, not a full referer URL including path/query. Since `request.referer` will typically be a full URL (e.g. `http://eviltrout.com/2013/...`), this can cause the resize message to fail/throw, breaking auto-resize. Although `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` requires a referer to be present, it does not ensure it is a valid `targetOrigin` value.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb`: `Discourse::InvalidParameters` on a missing arg will be retried forever (~25 times with exponential backoff) by Sidekiq's default retry behavior, producing noisy dead letters

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Jobs::RetrieveTopic#execute` raises `Discourse::InvalidParameters.new(:embed_url)` when `args[:embed_url]` is blank, but the only shown enqueue site (`EmbedController#best`) uses `params.require(:embed_url)` and passes `embed_url:` to `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`, so the job will not be enqueued without the arg based on this diff. Also, the finding’s claim of being retried “forever” is not supported by the diff; no Sidekiq retry configuration is shown here, and Sidekiq’s default behavior is finite retries, not infinite.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:38-45: test verifies mocks, not real behavior — mocks TopicRetriever.new and retriever.retrieve but the controller actually calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...); nothing verifies the job is enqueued with user_id/embed_url args or that the loading template is rendered

adjudication.rationale: The finding matches the diff: `EmbedController#best` enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: ..., embed_url: ...)` when `topic_id` is nil, and renders `loading` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb). However, the spec "tells the topic retriever to work when no previous embed is found" instead mocks `TopicRetriever.new` and expects `retriever.retrieve` (spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb). Since the controller never instantiates `TopicRetriever`, this test is asserting behavior that does not occur and would fail; it also doesn't verify the actual job enqueueing or loading template rendering.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/post_revisor.rb:85: skipping validations via @opts[:skip_validations] changes PostRevisor#revise! semantics for every caller, with zero test coverage for skip_validations or that normal revisions still validate

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes PostRevisor behavior: in lib/post_revisor.rb `@post.save` becomes `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, meaning callers passing `skip_validations: true` (newly used in TopicEmbed.import when revising imported content) will now bypass model validations whereas previously the option had no effect. That’s a nontrivial semantics change that should be covered by tests around validation vs skip_validations behavior. However, the finding’s claim of “zero test coverage” for this cannot be fully verified from the diff alone (pre-existing specs may exist outside the shown changes).

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb: perform_retrieve, retrieved_recently? (Redis 60-second $redis.setnx throttle including no_throttle staff bypass), and fetch_http are entirely untested; only the host-validation gate is covered

adjudication.rationale: The new `TopicRetriever` has nontrivial behavior in `retrieved_recently?` (Redis `setnx` + `expire` 60s throttle and `@opts[:no_throttle]` bypass), plus `perform_retrieve` branching (`TopicEmbed.exists?` short-circuit, optional `Jobs::PollFeed` execution, then `fetch_http` which calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote`). In `spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb`, tests only cover the host-validation gate (`invalid_host?`) and whether `perform_retrieve` is called based on a stubbed `retrieved_recently?`; they do not exercise the actual Redis throttle logic, the bypass option, or the `perform_retrieve`/`fetch_http` branches. This is a concrete testing gap for newly added logic, but not a direct defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb: tests only verify guard stubs; no coverage of RSS parsing (SimpleRSS.parse/open), link-vs-id URL fallback, CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub), or passing items to TopicEmbed.import

adjudication.rationale: In spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb, the tests only cover the guard conditions in execute (feed_polling_enabled?, feed_polling_url.present?, embed_by_username.present?) and that execute delegates to poll_feed. They do not exercise the substantive logic added in Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed: `SimpleRSS.parse open(...)`, the `url = i.link; url = i.id if url.blank? || url !~ /^https?\:\/\//` fallback, `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, or calling `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, i.title, content)` for each item. This is a concrete, diff-grounded gap in test coverage for newly introduced behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb: import_remote (readability-based extraction used by disqus task and TopicRetriever#fetch_http) has no coverage — no fixture HTML, no assertions on extracted title/content or Readability output

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds TopicEmbed.import_remote (uses ruby-readability + open(url).read, then TopicEmbed.import with doc.title/doc.content) in app/models/topic_embed.rb and it is invoked by both TopicRetriever#fetch_http and the disqus.thor task. The added spec spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb only covers TopicEmbed.import and does not exercise import_remote at all (no stubbing of open/read, no fixture HTML, no assertions about Readability::Document output). This is a specific, diff-grounded test coverage gap for newly added nontrivial logic, not a direct defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb: missing edge cases for absolutize_urls — nonstandard ports (prefix << ":#{port}" branch), protocol-relative //host/path links (silently left relative), and https with port 443 are untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial URL-rewriting logic in `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`: it appends a port to the prefix when `uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443` and only rewrites links when `href/src.start_with?('/')`. The accompanying spec (`spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb`) only exercises the basic case with an `http://eviltrout.com/123` base URL and `/...` relative paths; it does not cover the explicit nonstandard-port branch, nor the behavior for protocol-relative (`//host/path`) URLs which would not match `start_with?('/')` and thus remain unchanged. These are concrete, diff-grounded missing tests rather than a confirmed defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb: untested edge cases — referer host differing from embeddable_host, and malformed referer triggering the hand-written URI::InvalidURIError rescue in ensure_embeddable

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial authorization logic in `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` that rejects requests when `URI(request.referer).host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host` and rescues `URI::InvalidURIError` to raise `Discourse::InvalidAccess`. The new spec (`spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb`) tests missing referer and the success path where referer equals the embed_url, but it does not cover (1) a referer with a different host than `embeddable_host`, nor (2) a malformed referer that would exercise the `rescue URI::InvalidURIError` branch. This is a specific, diff-grounded missing test coverage concern rather than a demonstrated functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17: no tests for the new embed JS — the security-relevant origin check (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1), resize postMessage handler, and iframe construction are untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new client-side logic in `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js` (iframe construction with `iframe.src = discourseUrl + "embed/best?..."`, and a `window.addEventListener('message', ...)` handler that performs an origin check `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` and resizes the iframe). The diff also adds several Ruby specs, but no tests exercising this new JS behavior are present in the changes shown. Since this is new, security-relevant cross-window messaging logic, the lack of coverage is a concrete review concern grounded in the diff rather than a generic request.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No integration test for the end-to-end embed flow (EmbedController → job → TopicRetriever → TopicEmbed.import → /embed/best rendering); best.html.erb renders raw post.cooked with raw-HTML cook_method posts, a real unfiltered-HTML risk with no coverage

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a `raw_html` cook path that explicitly bypasses the rendering/sanitization pipeline (`Post#cook` returns `raw` when `cook_method == :raw_html`), and the embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: :raw_html` and feeds it `contents` originating from RSS (`Jobs::PollFeed` uses `i.content`), which is not sanitized in this diff. This is a concrete XSS/unfiltered-HTML exposure in the new embed flow, not just a lack of tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In embed_controller.rb ensure_embeddable: X-Frame-Options header is set before the rescue of URI::InvalidURIError, so the header is set even for rejected requests, and the guard logic and header side-effect are entangled in one method; restructure so URI parsing, access check, and header set are separate steps

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, `response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = "ALLOWALL"` is executed only after both guard checks succeed. If `URI(request.referer || '')` raises `URI::InvalidURIError`, control jumps to the `rescue` before the header assignment, so the header is not set for those rejected requests. Likewise, the explicit `raise Discourse::InvalidAccess` guard clauses occur before the header assignment. While one could argue about separating concerns, the finding’s core claim that the header is set even on rejected requests is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.html.erb embeds request.referer directly into inline JS via parent.postMessage without escaping, enabling script injection if the referer contains quotes or </script>; target origin should be derived from trusted SiteSetting.embeddable_host instead
matched_golden_ids: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that `request.referer` is interpolated into inline JavaScript without escaping, which can enable script injection/XSS if the referer contains malicious content (e.g., quotes or `</script>`). This is the same core issue as the golden comment, with an additional recommendation about trusted origin.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve executes Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) synchronously instead of enqueueing the job or extracting a shared feed-polling service, causing a full RSS feed re-parse and import of all feed items per embed request, defeating the per-URL throttle and coupling the retriever to the scheduled job's internals

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true it calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously (see `lib/topic_retriever.rb`) before falling back to HTTP fetch. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` parses the configured feed and iterates `rss.items.each` importing each item (`app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`). This is a real design/performance concern introduced by the diff: an embed request can trigger a full feed parse/import attempt and tightly couples the retriever to the scheduled job implementation, and the per-URL throttle (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`) doesn't prevent repeated full-feed work across different embed URLs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.import mutates the contents argument passed by the caller (contents << ... and absolutize_urls on the mutated string), breaking frozen strings and silently corrupting mutable ones; the sha1 is computed on the mutated content; should use local variables instead of mutating parameters

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, the method appends to the caller-provided `contents` string via `contents << "\n<hr>..."`, which mutates the argument in-place. This can cause unintended side effects for callers that reuse `contents`, and would raise an error if a frozen string is passed. The diff shows this mutation clearly; however, within this PR’s shown call sites (e.g., PollFeed building `content = ...` and import_remote using `doc.content`) it’s not verifiably causing broken behavior, so it’s better classified as a non-bug but real review concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Post#cook returns raw before applying Plugin::Filter :after_post_cook for raw_html posts, so plugins relying on after_post_cook (sanitization, link rewriting) silently don't run on RSS-imported posts

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/post.rb, Post#cook now immediately `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which bypasses `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)`. TopicEmbed.import creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, so RSS/imported posts will skip all `:after_post_cook` plugin hooks (including any sanitization/link rewriting done there) and `post.cooked` will equal `post.raw` (also asserted in spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb).

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed#absolutize_urls duplicates nearly identical fixup logic for a[href] and img[src], inviting drift and missing handling of srcset/protocol-relative URLs; collapse into a loop or helper

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, the diff shows two nearly identical blocks that rewrite relative URLs: one iterating `fragment.css('a')` to update `href`, and another iterating `fragment.css('img')` to update `src`. This duplication is real and could lead to maintenance drift if one path is updated without the other; factoring into a helper/loop would improve robustness. The mention of missing `srcset`/protocol-relative handling is an edge-case completeness concern rather than a directly verifiable defect, but it is grounded in the limited attribute handling shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicRetriever#fetch_http and Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed duplicate the embed_by_username user lookup (User.where(username_lower: ...)), with the setting doing double duty across three places; extract a single embed_user lookup module

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows duplicated logic to resolve the embedding user from the same site setting: Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed does `User.where(username_lower: SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase).first` and TopicRetriever#fetch_http does the same. This is a maintainability/architecture concern (DRY, single source of truth), not a functional defect. The finding’s mention of "three places" is a slight overstatement, but the core duplication across these two methods is verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicRetriever's Redis throttle uses non-atomic setnx followed by expire; a crash between them leaves a permanent throttle key blocking retrieval forever, and it couples to the global $redis handle; use SET with EX / nx: true, ex: 60

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb, retrieved_recently? sets a throttle key with `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and only afterwards applies TTL via `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. If the process crashes or is interrupted between these two calls, the key will remain without expiration, causing retrieval to be throttled permanently for that embed_url. This is a real correctness/availability bug introduced by the diff; using an atomic `SET` with `NX` and `EX` would avoid it. (The note about coupling to global `$redis` is also grounded, but the atomicity issue is the defect.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed#import interpolates the url into raw HTML ('<a href=\'#{url}\'>...') without escaping, and the https? regex permits characters like quotes and <, creating an injection path since posts are cooked as raw HTML and rendered raw; also a model layer doing HTML/view assembly

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the URL is only gated by `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which merely checks the prefix and would allow quotes/angle brackets in the remainder of the string. The code then interpolates `url` directly into an HTML snippet: `"#{url}"` and appends it to `contents`. Imported posts are created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` for that cook method, so no sanitization/rendering pipeline runs. Finally, the embed view renders `raw post.cooked`, making this a verifiable XSS/injection path introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: retrieve_topic.rb contains unused require_dependency 'email/sender' copied from another job template

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb`, the job file adds `require_dependency 'email/sender'`, but the `RetrieveTopic#execute` method only looks up a `User` and calls `TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve`; there is no reference to `Email::Sender` (or anything from `email/sender`) anywhere in this diff. This makes the finding of an unused/copy-pasted require verifiable from the changes, though it’s not a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Jobs::PollFeed#feed_key (with its memoization and require 'digest/sha1') is dead code, never called, implying caching behavior that doesn't exist

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the method `feed_key` (which memoizes `"feed-modified:#{Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(...)}`) is defined but nothing in this diff calls it. Likewise, `require 'digest/sha1'` is only used by `feed_key`. That makes the caching/throttling implication of `feed_key` effectively unused in the added implementation (at least within the PR’s changes), i.e., dead/unutilized code rather than an actual runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed/best.html.erb uses malformed/inverted conditional logic (<%- end if %>) with structurally identical branches, and can raise on @topic_view.topic when @topic_view is nil; simplify to a single link_to with a ternary i18n key

adjudication.rationale: In app/views/embed/best.html.erb the header block ends with `<%- end if %>`, which emits Ruby `end if` with no condition. That is invalid Ruby syntax and would cause the template to fail to compile/render when the `best` view is used. The claim about `@topic_view` being nil in this view is not supported by the controller (it renders `loading` when no topic_id), but the malformed ERB closing is a real defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Embed controller enqueues retrieve_topic then renders loading view, with the retry flow spread across three files (controller, job, client reload JS) with no shared contract; if the job takes >30s the user sees Loading forever; reload interval should be configurable/documented

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when no topic exists it enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb`, which hardcodes a `setTimeout(document.location.reload, 30000)`. This retry mechanism is indeed split across controller/job/view with no explicit shared contract (e.g., backoff, max retries, failure signaling), and the 30s interval is not configurable or documented in the diff. However, the claim that a job taking >30s causes “Loading forever” is not strictly verifiable: the page will keep reloading until the job completes, so it’s indefinite only if the job never succeeds.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unrelated force: true added to previously shipped create_top_topics migration is a latent data-drop hazard on partially-migrated DBs and obscures PR intent (along with whitespace-only migrate_word_counts.rb edit)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does modify an existing, timestamped migration that likely already shipped: `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` changes `create_table :top_topics` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`, which instructs Rails to drop the table before creating it. While this typically won’t affect already-migrated production DBs (the migration won’t re-run), it is a real, diff-grounded concern because editing old migrations and adding `force: true` can cause unexpected data loss on rebuilds/partial/incorrectly tracked migration states and obscures PR intent. The whitespace-only change in `20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb` is also present but is primarily noise.

adjudication_records.issue_text: create_table :topic_embeds uses force: true, which drops an existing topic_embeds table and its data if present, and inside change is recorded as a reversible create whose rollback would permanently drop the table — should be a plain create_table

adjudication.rationale: The new migration `db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb` does use `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`, which would drop and recreate the table if it already exists (risking data loss in non-fresh DBs). However, since this is introducing a brand-new table in a migration, the diff alone doesn’t prove an actual data-loss bug will occur in normal migration flow; it’s more a risky/unnecessary migration option than a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Adding force: true to the already-applied migration CreateTopTopics can drop the existing top_topics table with all its data if it re-executes; editing a historical migration is pure risk with no benefit and should be reverted

adjudication.rationale: The diff edits an existing migration `20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` drops the table if it already exists before recreating it. Since this is a historical migration (not a new one), any scenario where migrations are re-run against a DB that already has `top_topics` (e.g., resetting/redoing migrations, partial restores, or running in an environment with the table preexisting) could silently drop the table and lose data. That risk is introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_column :posts :cook_method uses hardcoded default: 1 instead of Post.cook_methods[:regular], so if the enum ordering changes, existing rows silently change meaning

adjudication.rationale: The migration `AddCookMethodToPosts` hardcodes `default: 1` for `:cook_method` (db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb), while the meaning of `1` is implicitly tied to `Post.cook_methods ||= Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)` in `app/models/post.rb`. This isn’t an immediate defect given the current enum ordering, but it is a diff-grounded maintainability/data-compatibility risk: if the enum definition/order changes later, existing rows with value `1` could be reinterpreted without any DB change. (Using the enum constant in a migration is also nontrivial, but the finding’s core concern about coupling to numeric ordering is valid.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embeds.topic_id and post_id are null: false but lack foreign-key constraints, so deleting a topic or post leaves orphaned embed records that cause EmbedController#best to raise a 500

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateTopicEmbeds` creates `topic_embeds` with `topic_id` and `post_id` set `null: false` but adds no foreign-key constraints or dependent cleanup (`add_index` only on `embed_url`). That can allow orphaned `topic_embeds` rows if a `Topic` or `Post` is deleted later. However, the claim that this *will* cause `EmbedController#best` to raise a 500 is not directly verifiable from the diff: `best` only plucks a `topic_id` (`TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed`) and then calls `TopicView.new(...)`, but the diff doesn’t show how `TopicView` behaves when the topic is missing (could be handled or could error). So the missing FK/orphan risk is real and diff-grounded, but the asserted 500 is not proven here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stored XSS via raw_html cook method: article's raw HTML inserted directly as cooked and rendered with raw, with no sanitization; Readability's tag whitelist permits javascript: and data: URIs in a[href]/img[src] (app/models/post.rb:131, app/views/embed/best.html.erb:18)

adjudication.rationale: Diff introduces a `raw_html` cook_method where `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly (`return raw if cook_method == ...`), bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline (app/models/post.rb). Imported feed/remote content is stored as `raw` with `cook_method: :raw_html` (TopicEmbed.import) and then rendered with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in the embed view (app/views/embed/best.html.erb). `TopicEmbed.import_remote` allows ``/`` with `href`/`src` attributes and there is no URI scheme sanitization shown, so malicious HTML/JS could be persisted and executed when embedded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: HTML injection via unescaped URL interpolation in the 'imported from' footer: url only prefix-validated and interpolated raw into a raw_html post (app/models/topic_embed.rb:11)

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code appends raw HTML containing the unescaped `url` into `contents`: `I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}")`. The only validation is `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent quotes/angle brackets in the remainder of the string (e.g., `http://example.com' onclick='...`). Because the post is created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `Post#cook` returns `raw` for `raw_html`, this HTML is rendered without sanitization (and the embed view uses `<%= raw post.cooked %>`), enabling HTML/attribute injection.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) in poll_feed.rb:33 re-materializes escaped HTML entities like <script> into live tags, re-arming escaped HTML

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` will turn escaped entities (e.g. `<script>`) back into literal tags. That content is then imported via `TopicEmbed.import`, which creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. `Post#cook` explicitly returns `raw` for `:raw_html`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline, and `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` renders `raw post.cooked`. Together, this can re-arm escaped HTML from the feed into executable markup (XSS) in the embedded/comments output.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Referer check is weak/case-sensitive host equality and the embed endpoint trusts the client for both referer and embed_url; also post.message targetOrigin uses request.referer, allowing spoofed referer to redirect disclosure to attacker origins (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:28, layouts/embed.html.erb:9)

adjudication.rationale: In `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb`, the iframe posts a message using `parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>')`. `targetOrigin` must be an origin (scheme+host+port) or `*`, not a full referer URL with path/query, so this is likely to throw or prevent the resize message from being delivered, breaking embedding behavior. Additionally, `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` authorizes solely by `URI(request.referer).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, which is a direct string equality (case-sensitive) and relies on a client-supplied Referer header, making the check fragile and potentially spoofable outside normal browser embedding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: postMessage origin check in embed.js uses substring match (indexOf) instead of strict origin equality; also iframe.src concatenation breaks if discourseUrl lacks trailing slash (app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:19)

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js, the message origin check is `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`, which is a substring test rather than strict origin equality, so an attacker origin that is a prefix of `discourseUrl` could pass. Also `iframe.src = discourseUrl + "embed/best?..."` will produce an invalid URL when `discourseUrl` lacks a trailing `/` (e.g., `https://forum.example.comembed/best`). Both are real behavior/security/correctness issues visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Silent-pass/infinite loading loop: retrieve fails silently on invalid host, missing embed user, feed fetch failure, etc., while the client reloads every 30s forever with no error signal, re-enqueueing jobs each reload (embed_controller.rb:12-15, topic_retriever.rb:16-20, loading.html.erb:6-10)

adjudication.rationale: The diff implements a loading page that unconditionally reloads every 30s (app/views/embed/loading.html.erb) whenever no TopicEmbed exists (EmbedController#best). In that state, the controller also enqueues :retrieve_topic on every request. However, the job can “do nothing” without surfacing any error back to the client: TopicRetriever#retrieve returns early if invalid_host? is true (topic_retriever.rb:16-20), and invalid_host? compares SiteSetting.embeddable_host to the *embed_url* host (not the referer). Since ensure_embeddable only validates the referer host, a valid embedding page could pass the filter while supplying an embed_url whose host differs, causing the retriever to silently skip retrieval forever. Similarly, fetch_http returns if embed_by_username is missing/invalid (topic_retriever.rb), leaving the embed absent and the iframe stuck in an infinite reload loop with repeated enqueues/throttled no-ops.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.import check-then-act race: concurrent RetrieveTopic jobs can create duplicate topics, with both running PostCreator side effects inside the transaction before the unique index aborts; should use create! rescue/upsert (app/models/topic_embed.rb:13-26)

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, the existence check (`embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first`) followed by creation inside the `if embed.blank?` branch is not atomic. With concurrent imports for the same `embed_url`, both can observe no row and both run `PostCreator#create` before attempting `TopicEmbed.create!`. The unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url` will then raise on the loser, and this code does not rescue it, causing the job/request to error (even if the DB transaction rolls back the topic/post). This is a real race introduced/exposed by the diff.
